meta.title: See the agents working in this checkout today

security.label: Step with an evidenced pain point

nodes.label: Agent runs in checkout
nodes.explanation: An agent counts when its working directory is inside this checkout, subdirectories included: the chat's own agent, or Claude Code, Codex, Pi or OpenCode started in a terminal. An agent's subagents fold into the session that started them. The whole feature needs [devtools.chat].enabled; the toolbar polls only while chat is on.

sources.label: Docs: which agents count; needs chat on
List polls only while chat is enabled

nodes.label: Scan agents in checkout
nodes.explanation: While chat is on and the page is visible, the toolbar asks GET /__devhost__/agents every 10 seconds. The control server scans every agent on the machine through agent-watcher (one scan shared for 5 s, 10 s timeout), keeps the top-level sessions whose working directory is inside the page's checkout (the project root of its routed service), and sorts waiting first, then working, unknown and idle. Rows carry the raw harness id, the session name, the path relative to the checkout and the last activity; transcript paths and native session ids stay on the server. When a harness cannot be scanned (a session store devhost cannot read, or the 10 s limit), the server still answers 200 with the agents it found and adds 'Some agents could not be listed.', but the page's schema strips that field and nothing reads it: the partial list replaces the last one and reads as complete, chat's check for another agent before a new conversation trusts it too, and the failure shows only as a 'running agents scan failed' log line repeated on every request (reload-and-agents-09).

sources.label: Poll every 10 s while the page is visible
Keep top-level agents inside the checkout
Answers the list, plus error on a failed scan

nodes.label: Running agents: N
nodes.explanation: With one or more agents in the checkout the toolbar shows a bot icon and the count, with a spinner while any agent works; its accessible name is 'Running agents: N' in every state. An agent waiting for approval gets the same idle bot icon as an idle agent, and with chat collapsed the Chat button shows the same spinner for waiting as for working, so an agent blocked on the person looks busy or idle (chat-approvals-03, owned by agent-chat). Each time the control appears or disappears, the right-anchored toolbar shifts sideways (reload-and-agents-05).

sources.label: Trigger: spinner only for working, count
Control placed in the toolbar

nodes.label: Agents in this checkout
nodes.explanation: Clicking the count opens the popover 'Agents in this checkout'. Each row reads harness, session name and 'this chat' over state, subdirectory and last activity, for example 'claude-code · project-37 · this chat' over 'Waiting for approval · . · just now': the raw harness id instead of Claude Code, a session name the CLI generated, '.' for the checkout root, and no action, not even Open Chat for this chat's own agent. With chat docked open, the popover opens underneath the chat panel and only fragments stay visible, so neither the rows nor Watch Live Activity can be used without closing chat (reload-and-agents-05; the docked-chat placement is its toolbar-shell slice). The list only reports and sends nothing to an agent.

sources.label: Rows: raw harness, name, state, subdirectory
Row data: raw ids, '.' for the root

nodes.label: Watch Live Activity
nodes.explanation: The link under the list opens a new tab on the control server's own address, http://127.0.0.1:<port>/__devhost__/agents/activity, with the page URL and chat target in the query. The server answers only a direct request from its own machine (a routed hostname gets 403 'Agent activity opens from the running agents list.'), with no-store and no-referrer, because transcripts can hold secrets. A page opened from another computer still lists the agents and shows the link, which opens that computer's own 127.0.0.1: a connection error, or whatever listens on that port there gets the page URL, and nothing says the page opens only on the stack's machine (reload-and-agents-13). The page shows a Live or Reconnecting badge and, until events arrive, 'Waiting for activity. Events appear here as agents work.' The port is an ephemeral one each run picks, and it closes with that run: after Ctrl-C, devhost stop, the idle timeout or devhost stack restart, the server closes the stream with 1001, the page retries the old port every 10 s without end, the badge reads Reconnecting forever, a restarted stack is never reached, and nothing says the stack stopped (reload-and-agents-10).

sources.label: Activity URL on the control origin
Direct local requests only; page render
Header, Live badge, empty state

nodes.label: Tail agent transcripts
nodes.explanation: Each open page gets its own WebSocket and its own agent-watcher run, with cursors in a temporary directory: it starts at the end of every transcript (no history), rescans every 5 seconds and keeps the top-level agents inside the checkout. Each event becomes harness, PID, event type, time, role, tool name, error flag and the content or tool output cut at 4096 characters; the tool input (the command or file) is not forwarded. Closing the tab ends the run and deletes its cursors.

sources.label: Per-page watcher from the end of transcripts
Event fields; text cut at 4096 characters

nodes.label: Read event lines
nodes.explanation: Events arrive newest first, at most 500. Each line joins time, raw harness id, raw event type, tool name and role, for example '2:10:47 PM · claude-code · tool_call · Edit · assistant': no command, file path or diff, so a harmless read and a destructive command look alike until a later result. Tool output and denials read 'tool_result · user', as if the person wrote them; replies arrive as unrendered Markdown; the PID each event carries is never shown, so two Claude Code agents interleave indistinguishably. An agent blocked on an approval never shows as waiting, although the toolbar list knows it (reload-and-agents-06).

sources.label: Line: time, harness, type, tool, role
Newest first, at most 500 events

nodes.label: Control disappears
nodes.explanation: With no agent in the checkout the control renders nothing: there is no empty state, so 'no agents' and 'agents devhost cannot see' look the same, and because the toolbar is anchored at its right edge, the stack name, service dots and branch move sideways each time the first agent starts or the last one stops (reload-and-agents-05). A scan that fails for the harness of every agent in the checkout ends here too, as if none ran (reload-and-agents-09). Saving [devtools.chat] enabled = false in devhost.toml removes the count, the list and their routes on the next health message, with no notice, while the agent keeps running (chat-approvals-08, owned by agent-chat).

sources.label: Renders nothing at zero agents
Chat off empties the list
Agent routes answer 404 while chat is off

nodes.label: Old checkout's agents
nodes.explanation: Worktrees > Switch and restart stack restarts the stack in another checkout with one click and no warning, although this list knows an agent there is working or waiting (chat-checkout-switch-02, owned by worktree-switch). The list then resolves the page's newly selected checkout and keeps only agents inside it, so an agent still working, or waiting for an approval, in the previous checkout drops out of the count and the list while it keeps running; chat hides its conversation the same way, and only switching back shows it again (chat-checkout-switch-01, owned by agent-chat).

sources.label: Root follows the page's selected checkout
Agents outside that root are skipped
Switch restarts the stack; names no agents

cards.title: What already works
items: Lists agents devhost did not start, from chat or a terminal (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode), counting subdirectories and folding subagents into their parent
Waiting agents sort first, then working, unknown and idle; the chat's own agent is marked this chat
One machine-wide scan serves every page for 5 s and runs only while a page is visible; transcript paths and native session ids never reach the app's origin
Watch Live Activity stays on 127.0.0.1 with no-store and no-referrer because transcripts can hold secrets, and its watcher stops when the tab closes
The list only reports: it never sends anything to an agent or answers its approvals

cards.title: Tickets on this journey
items: reload-and-agents-05 The list opens under docked chat; rows show claude-code, a generated session name and '.' with no Open Chat; the control vanishes at zero and shifts the toolbar
reload-and-agents-06 Watch Live Activity shows tool names without commands or files, labels tool output user, prints raw tokens and never shows an agent waiting for approval
reload-and-agents-09 A harness devhost cannot scan is never mentioned: the list reads as complete, and when it misses every agent the control vanishes as if none ran

reload-and-agents-10 After the stack stops, an open activity tab says Reconnecting forever: it retries the stopped run's 127.0.0.1 port, never reaches the restarted stack and never says the stack stopped

reload-and-agents-13 On a page opened from another computer, Watch Live Activity opens that computer's own 127.0.0.1, so it fails or reaches whatever listens there, and nothing says it opens only on the stack's machine
chat-approvals-03 A waiting agent's trigger looks the same as an idle one; only the open list says Waiting for approval (owned by agent-chat)
chat-approvals-08 Turning chat off in devhost.toml removes the count and list without a word while the agent keeps running (owned by agent-chat)
chat-checkout-switch-01 After Switch and restart stack, a working or waiting agent of the previous checkout drops out of the list while it keeps running (owned by agent-chat)
chat-checkout-switch-02 Switch and restart stack gives no warning about a working or waiting agent (owned by worktree-switch)

cards.title: Evidence
items: Traced from alexgorbatchev/devhost at edb5c0fc01cabae490e92ac23d4c785ec896c4ed; the review exercised build 0.0.12 live with Claude Code (Haiku): the chat agent seen Working, Waiting for approval and Idle, the list with chat docked, Watch Live Activity during and after a turn, Close Conversation, chat turned off in devhost.toml, and a switch with a waiting agent; a terminal Claude Code left at its untrusted-folder screen was not listed, because it writes no session file there. This diagram was traced from source only.
